question: Which of the following is the primary natural source of heat for the Earth?
options: The Sun
An electric heater
A burning candle
The Moon
answer: The Sun

question: Which action generates heat through friction?
options: Rubbing two hands together vigorously
Holding an ice cube in a cup
Switching off a table lamp
Pouring cold water into a glass
answer: Rubbing two hands together vigorously

question: What is the definition of the temperature of an object?
options: A measurement of its degree of hotness
The total amount of heat energy inside it
The time taken for an object to melt
The size and weight of the object
answer: A measurement of its degree of hotness

question: Which statement correctly describes heat?
options: Heat is a form of energy
Heat is measured using a measuring cylinder
Heat is the same thing as temperature
Heat always flows from cold objects to hot objects
answer: Heat is a form of energy

question: What is the main difference between heat and temperature?
options: Heat is a form of energy, while temperature is a measure of degree of hotness
Heat is measured in degree Celsius, while temperature is measured in Joules
Temperature flows from hot to cold, while heat stays inside an object
Temperature increases when heat is lost, while heat increases when temperature drops
answer: Heat is a form of energy, while temperature is a measure of degree of hotness

question: Beaker A contains 500 ml of water at 80°C. Beaker B contains 100 ml of water at 80°C. Which statement is correct?
options: Both beakers have the same temperature, but Beaker A contains more heat energy
Beaker A has a higher temperature than Beaker B
Beaker B contains more heat energy because it has less water
Both beakers contain the exact same amount of heat energy
answer: Both beakers have the same temperature, but Beaker A contains more heat energy

question: A hot metal rod at 90°C is placed into a basin of water at 25°C. In which direction does heat flow?
options: From the hot metal rod to the cooler water
From the cooler water to the hot metal rod
Heat flows back and forth equally between both
No heat flows because both are solids and liquids
answer: From the hot metal rod to the cooler water

question: When Meiling holds an ice cube in her bare hand, the ice cube begins to melt. Why?
options: The ice cube gains heat from her warmer hand
Coldness leaves the ice cube and enters her hand
Her hand loses temperature to the surrounding air
The ice cube loses heat to her hand
answer: The ice cube gains heat from her warmer hand

question: What happens to the temperature of an object when it LOSES heat?
options: Its temperature decreases
Its temperature increases
Its temperature remains unchanged
Its temperature rises then drops suddenly
answer: Its temperature decreases

question: What happens to the temperature of a cup of water when it GAINS heat?
options: Its temperature increases
Its temperature decreases
Its temperature drops to 0°C
Its temperature remains constant
answer: Its temperature increases

question: A mug of hot milo at 85°C is left on a dining table in a room at 28°C. When will heat stop flowing from the mug to the room?
options: When the milo cools down to 28°C
When the milo reaches 0°C
When all the milo evaporates
After exactly 5 minutes
answer: When the milo cools down to 28°C

question: A glass of cold milk at 5°C is left on a table in a room at 30°C. What happens to the milk over time?
options: It gains heat from the surroundings until its temperature reaches 30°C
It loses heat to the surroundings until its temperature reaches 0°C
It gains heat until its temperature reaches 100°C
Its temperature stays at 5°C indefinitely
answer: It gains heat from the surroundings until its temperature reaches 30°C

question: Two metal blocks, Block X (50°C) and Block Y (50°C), are placed in direct contact. Which statement about heat flow is correct?
options: No net heat flows between X and Y because they are at the same temperature
Heat flows from Block X to Block Y continuously
Heat flows from Block Y to Block X continuously
Both blocks lose heat until they reach 0°C
answer: No net heat flows between X and Y because they are at the same temperature

question: Which instrument is specifically used to measure temperature?
options: Thermometer
Measuring cylinder
Spring balance
Stopwatch
answer: Thermometer

question: What is the standard unit of measurement for temperature commonly used in Singapore schools?
options: Degree Celsius (°C)
Joule (J)
Centimeter (cm)
Grams (g)
answer: Degree Celsius (°C)

question: How should a student position his line of sight when reading a liquid-in-glass thermometer?
options: Level with the top of the liquid column
Looking down from above the thermometer
Looking up from below the thermometer bulb
At any convenient angle
answer: Level with the top of the liquid column

question: What is a major advantage of using a datalogger with a temperature sensor instead of a glass thermometer?
options: It can record continuous temperature changes automatically over time
It does not require any power or batteries to function
It makes the liquid inside heat up much faster
It turns heat energy directly into light
answer: It can record continuous temperature changes automatically over time

question: A warm metal spoon is placed into a bowl of cold ice cream. What happens to the spoon?
options: The spoon loses heat energy and its temperature decreases
The spoon gains heat energy and its temperature increases
The spoon loses coldness and its temperature increases
The spoon keeps its heat energy and temperature unchanged
answer: The spoon loses heat energy and its temperature decreases

question: Which electrical appliance is designed specifically to produce heat as its main function?
options: An electric bread toaster
An electric ceiling fan
A digital wristwatch
A television screen
answer: An electric bread toaster

question: When a student steps out of a swimming pool on a windy day, she feels cold. Why?
options: Water on her skin gains heat from her body to evaporate, causing her body to lose heat
Coldness from the air enters her body directly through her skin
Her body temperature rises rapidly in the wind
The swimming pool water transfers heat into her body
answer: Water on her skin gains heat from her body to evaporate, causing her body to lose heat

question: A laboratory thermometer is moved from room-temperature air into a beaker of hot water. Why does the liquid column inside the thermometer rise?
options: The liquid gains heat from the hot water and expands
The liquid loses heat to the hot water and contracts
The glass tube contracts and squeezes the liquid upward
Air enters the bulb and pushes the liquid upward
answer: The liquid gains heat from the hot water and expands

question: Cup A contains 100 ml of water at 90°C. Cup B contains 100 ml of water at 40°C. Which statement is true?
options: Cup A contains more heat energy than Cup B
Cup B contains more heat energy than Cup A
Both cups contain the same amount of heat energy
Neither cup contains any heat energy
answer: Cup A contains more heat energy than Cup B

question: A hot copper key at 70°C is dropped into a beaker of water at 25°C. Which row correctly describes the heat changes?
options: Copper key loses heat; Water gains heat
Copper key gains heat; Water loses heat
Both copper key and water gain heat
Both copper key and water lose heat
answer: Copper key loses heat; Water gains heat

question: Heat will continue to flow between two objects placed in contact until:
options: Both objects reach the exact same temperature
One object reaches 0°C and the other reaches 100°C
All heat energy in both objects is completely used up
The smaller object absorbs all heat from the larger object
answer: Both objects reach the exact same temperature
